_meta.doc: Marquee Entry cinematics (P2a-special): static, aura-independent title cards for the league's marquee fights. Keyed by the battle row's event name. Each entry: kicker (small letterspaced header), epithet (one italic framing line), lines (2-3 beats the foe speaks — the nameplate shows the rolled trainer's name at runtime, so write role-generic). No choices, no Vibe Exchange, no buff — gravity preserved. A missing/malformed key falls back to the legacy timed VS splash. The Mystery Figure is deliberately ABSENT: its bespoke pre-boss cinematic + identity intro quotes already own that entrance.
_meta.editing: Add or rewrite entries freely — strings render verbatim (HTML-escaped). Keep lines ≤ ~110 chars.

Victory Road.epithet: The mountain doesn't care how you got here. Only how you leave.
lines: Eight badges gets you through that door. It doesn't get you up this road.
Everyone you'll meet from here on came to end somebody's story. Mind it isn't yours.

E1.epithet: Past this point, the league keeps score forever.
lines: Welcome, challenger. Your badges bought you this room — nothing in it.
I am the first of four. Most stories end with me. Let's read yours.

E2.epithet: One down. The hall behind you is longer than the hall ahead.
lines: You beat the first? Good. They soften challengers up for me.
No healing crowds, no second chances. Just you, me, and the door you can't reopen.

E3.epithet: This deep in, talent stops mattering. Preparation is everything.
lines: Two doors down. You're tired. I'm not. That's the whole strategy.
The third room is where champions are made — or where they're quietly returned.

E4.epithet: Behind me there is only the chair, and the one who sits in it.
lines: I am the last wall. Every challenger who reached the Champion went through me first.
Show me everything. If you hold anything back, you'll carry it home unspent.

Champion.epithet: The chair is heavier than it looks. Come take it anyway.
lines: So it's you. The Four spoke well of you — they speak well of no one.
This room remembers every battle ever fought in it. Give it one worth keeping.
When the dust settles, one of us hands the other a title. Begin.
